State of Maine
DEPARTMENT OF EDUCATION
Testimony of Courtney Belolan, Director of Policy and Government Affairs
In Support of: L.D. 86
An Act to Update the Laws Regarding Education
Before the Joint Standing Committee on Education and Cultural Affairs
Sponsored by: Representative Sargent
Date: April 1, 2025
Senator Rafferty, Representative Murphy, and Members of the Joint Standing Committee on Education and Cultural Affairs:
My name is Courtney Belolan, and I am here today representing the Department of Education speaking in support of LD 86, An Act to Update the Laws Regardmg Education which proposes to amend statute to provide alignment with Federal policy and clarity on previously enacted financial statutes.
The Department seeks two changes to align our practice with Federal policy. First, we ask that the statutory definition of homeless student be updated to match the federal definition by removmg the inclusion of students awaiting foster placement. This change will align the language of the Maine Department of Education with the nationally recognized language.
Second, we propose an update to statute regarding private schools' receipt of public funds for tuition purposes. This change reflects the United States Supreme Court's 2022 Carson v. Makin decision by removing nonsectarian from the eligibility requirements.
We also propose an update to the statutes relating to community school districts to allow for reorganization without the need for a private and special law. Currently, a community school district is the only type of school that needs a private or special law to reorganize.
For clarity on financial statutes, the Department notes updating audit report statutes for education service centers and school administrative units to reduce duplicative audit submissions. We also request that Title 20-A, Chapter 608 be repealed. This chapter has been replaced by various sections of Title 20-A, Chapter 606-B, the Essential Programs and Services Funding Act. The calculations as written m the remammg section of Chapter 608 are provided for in Chapter 606-B. Maintaining the redundant statute has caused confusion as people seek understanding to make important decisions about school finance.
For these reasons, the Department of Education is in support of L.D. 86, An Act to Update the Laws Regarding Education that was developed in order to provide clarity to our statutes. I would be happy to answer any questions the Committee may have and can be available for work sessions on this bill.

Testimony of Rep. Holly T. Sargent introducing
LD 86, An Act to Update the Laws Regarding Education Before the Joint Standing Committee on Education and Cultural Affairs

Senator Rafferty, Representative Murphy and distinguished colleagues of the Joint Standing Committee on Education and Cultural Affairs, I apologize that I am not with you today to introduce LD 86 on behalf of the Department of Education, and I thank our colleague for presenting in my place.
This bill amends a number of areas in statute including eliminating several outdated provisions. The changes span many MSRS 20-A chapters and the reasons for the necessity of these changes vary from updates to match changes in Federal language, to removing statute that has been rendered obsolete by newer statute.
The Department of Education will present testimony on this bill and detail the changes. I respectfully request that you defer any specific questions regarding the content to them.
Thank you for your consideration of this bill.

Dear Senator Joseph Rafferty, Representative Kelly Murphy, and Members of the Education and Cultural Affairs Committee:
I am Pamela Doyen, RSU 56 Superintendent of Schools and the President of the Western Maine Regional Service Center (WMRSC). WMRSC formed in 2021 and currently has 12 members: Andover School Department; Fayette School Department; Lisbon School Department; MSAD 13; MSAD 59; RSU 9, RSU 10, RSU 44; RSU 56; RSU 58; RSU 73; and RSU 74.
I am writing on behalf of all WMRSC members in support of LD 86, "An Act To Update the Laws Regarding Education." Specifically, we urge the Committee to pass the Department of Education's proposed addition of language in Sec. 6. 20-A MRSA �3804, which provides for a service center, under the fiscal agency of a school administrative unit, to be included in the annual audit of that school administrative unit and not be required to file an additional audit.
Approval of this language is significant to a service center's overall operating budget. In our case, if we are unnecessarily required to pay for a separate, independent audit, the projected cost would be $7500 vs. $1200 if we are able to have the audit conducted as part of our fiscal agent's annual audit. Note that we are one of several service centers across Maine; the price of not supporting this update to the statutory language would end up costing the collective group of service centers tens of thousands of dollars in any given year. Those funds would be much better spent on Maine's students and teachers.
On behalf of all WMRSC members, I thank the Committee for your consideration of supporting LD 86.
Sincerely,
Pamela Doyen, Ph.D. Superintendent, RSU 56 President, WMRSC
